history.content: Tell me about the reason of the India Movement

One of the most important events of the 19th century was the rise of Indian nationalism, leading Indians to seek first "self-rule" and later "complete independence". Historians are divided over the causes of its rise, but probable reasons include a "clash of interests of the Indian people with British interests", "racial discriminations", and "the revelation of India's past". Strategies involved boycotting British products and the revival of domestic products and production processes.
I also heard that there were some paralel movements involved in Indian independence.

Yes, you're correct. The Swadeshi movement, also known as Vandemataram movement in deltaic Andhra Pradesh ,was a part of the Indian independence movement and the developing Indian nationalism. It was an economic strategy aimed at removing the British Empire from power and improving economic conditions in India by following the principles of swadeshi. The Swadeshi movement had five phases and involved boycotting British products and the revival of domestic products and production processes. Some of the prominent leaders of this movement were Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, Lala Lajpat Rai, V.O. Chidambaram Pillai, Sri Aurobindo, Surendranath Banerji, and Rabindranath Tagore.
Is the Swadeshi movement the only one? What about the Quit Movement?  It is part of the India Nationalist movements.

No, the Swadeshi movement is not the only nationalist movement in India. Another significant movement was the Quit India Movement, also known as the India August Movement. This movement was launched at the Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee by Mahatma Gandhi on 8 August 1942, during World War II, demanding an end to British Rule of India.The Quit India Movement was opposed by several political groups during the Indian Independence Movement, including the Muslim League, the Hindu Mahasabha, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, the Communist Party of India, and the princely states. The movement had less support in the princely states, as the princes were strongly opposed and funded the opposition.

You're welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify the differences between the Swadeshi movement and the Quit India Movement, and provide more context on their roles in the Indian independence movement. If you have any other questions, feel free to ask!
How did the nationalist movements worked in India? Was the population realy involved?

Yes, the population was significantly involved in the nationalist movements in India. These movements were often organized as mass movements that emphasized and raised questions concerning the interests of the Indian people. People were encouraged to take action themselves, and the movements sparked nationalist sentiment among the populace. Figures like Mahatma Gandhi united the nation behind his non-violent philosophy and put pressure on the British occupation. While the movements failed to win independence for India in their primary objective, they did contribute to a growing sense of nationalism and unity among the Indian people. Economic factors and united resistance also played a role in drawing attention to the British failures to achieve solidarity over India, ultimately leading to India's independence in 1947.
